### 1. Project

Ref YMCA-YAR-RFP · Issued 2026-10-12 · Closes 2026-10-30 · Contact Project manager, pm@example.com

YMCA NSW intends to extend Accommodation lodges (Class 3) and Conference hall (Class 9b) at Springwood Rd, Yarramundi NSW (Hawkesbury).

| The building | Site and planning | Delivery |
|---|---|---|
| Work type: Extension / addition | Site address: Springwood Rd, Yarramundi NSW | Client: YMCA NSW |
| Building: Accommodation lodges: Class 3; Conference hall: Class 9b | Local government area: Hawkesbury | Procurement route: Design and construct; this appointment is novated to the contractor |
| Car parks: 129 | Site area: 216,000 m² | Regulated design applies: Yes |
|  | Planning pathway: Development application (DA) |  |

Conditions that apply: Flood-affected site; Work to an existing building; Site stays occupied or operating during the works; Delivered in stages; Several buildings or a campus; Parts with different NCC classes; Drinking water catchment (neutral or beneficial effect); Works in a public road or intersection.
Conditions not yet known: Contaminated or potentially contaminated land; Acid sulfate soils mapped; Groundwater above the base of excavation; Basement or deep excavation; Excavation next to adjoining structures or boundaries; Existing on-site detention to keep or modify; On-site detention required by council; Council requires stormwater quality modelling.

Information provided: 30 current documents in the project register, listed in the issue record

### 2. Your role

Civil engineer for work outside building footprints: earthworks, roads and pavements, levels, stormwater and water quality. The hydraulic engineer designs roof drainage, downpipes and pumped systems; utility designers do water, sewer, power and communications; you combine their layouts with yours. The traffic engineer sets parking numbers, design vehicles and intersection layout; you design to them.
After novation you are engaged by the head contractor. Price the stages before and after novation separately.
Design vehicle: 14.5 m rigid bus

### 3. Scope by stage

Each design stage is issued as one draft and one final. Design stages are priced by element so firms can be compared line by line. Options are priced on their own and are not in the base fee.

| Stage | Deliverable at sign-off |
|---|---|
| Schematic design for planning approval | Review of information; site visit; survey and services gap analysis (BYDA, existing utilities plan); review of 4 architect layouts; 2 civil options, then one agreed concept; pre-DA meeting; DA drawings and civil report; stormwater drainage model; combined utility plan |
| Design for the D&C tender | Design developed to the approved plans and consent conditions as far as the D&C tender needs; performance specification; schedule of the design you retain and the design the contractor completes. You hold the design to tender issue; the contractor holds it after award. |
| Final design after novation (option) | Construction set and construction certificate issue for the contractor after novation. The contractor holds the design after novation.. A later stage the client may commission. |
| Construction phase (option) | 6 inspections at hold points (subgrade, pipes, pavement); RFIs up to 10 hours; input to 2 construction certificate(s) and 1 occupation certificate; certificate to the certifier based on the inspections made. A later stage the client may commission. |
| As-built and completion (option) | Review of the surveyor's works-as-executed survey; as-built drawings; detention system certification; maintenance information; support for title, covenant or public-asset handover where it applies; final certificate. With the construction phase. |

Elements priced in the design stages:
A Earthworks and sediment control: Bulk earthworks, cut and fill volumes; erosion and sediment control; building pads.
B Roads pavements and levels: Internal road and car park geometry; finished levels; pavement profiles from the geotechnical report; signage and line marking; turning paths; retaining wall geometry and levels outside buildings; accessible path grades.
C Stormwater: Drainage outside building footprints; overland flow; detention and water quality where section 5 includes them.
D Public road works: Intersection or driveway design to Austroads and the traffic engineer's advice; submission for council or TfNSW approval.

### 4. Allowances

Price exactly these. Work beyond an allowance needs a written instruction (section 6) and is then charged at your R3 rates.

| Item | Allowance | Item | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design meetings | 10 per design stage, up to 2 hours, online | Authority meetings | 3 |
| Site visits during design | 2 | Architect layouts reviewed | 4 |
| Civil concept options | 2, then one agreed | Drawing revisions before lodgement | 2 |

| Construction RFIs | 10 hours | Construction certificate inputs | 2, and 1 occupation certificate |

### 5. Scope position

Service levels are set for a complex project (Site area over 20,000); technical items follow the project's own facts.
Included in the fee: Combined utility plan from others' layouts; Discharge point, downstream capacity, easements and approvals confirmed at schematic design; Stormwater drainage model (DRAINS or equal); Hydraulic-to-civil connections: location, levels and who designs each side; Water quality modelling (MUSIC) and treatment design; Neutral or beneficial effect assessment (drinking water catchment); Feasibility of keeping or modifying the existing on-site detention; Investigation brief for retained drainage and services (CCTV, survey, potholing) and how findings change the design; Geotechnical and environmental advice coordinated into earthworks reuse and disposal (balance depends on material suitability); Flood: floor levels and flood report for the application; Authority submission schedule: designer, review rounds, asset handover; Coordinated 3D civil model (surface and earthworks); Design criteria document; Civil safety in design report; Civil design compliance declarations for the regulated designs.
Optional: price each on its own line in R1: Replacement on-site detention design, pending the feasibility assessment (Price replacement design as an option pending the feasibility assessment); On-site detention design (needed if council requires on-site detention); Flood evacuation plan; Detailed pavement design where the geotechnical report does not give it (name the designer in R4); 3D clash check of combined services; Water management strategy (supply, reuse, effluent); Audit of the contractor's quality system; Shoring, rock anchors, slope stability (needed only for deep excavation or unstable slopes); Trunk drainage, external catchments, watercourse works; Road safety audit by an auditor independent of the design; Operation and maintenance manual for stormwater devices.
Excluded: the party named does it: Structural design of retaining walls (structural engineer, not yet engaged); Locating services; designing service relocations (services locator and utility designers, not yet engaged); Authority asset approvals (specialist engineering assessment) (structural engineer, not yet engaged); Pre-tender estimate or bill of quantities (quantity surveyor, not yet engaged); Modification applications (town planner, not yet engaged).
Tell us in R6 if you disagree with any line. Do not add your own general exclusions; any you add are treated as non-compliant.

### 6. Terms

- Engagement is under AS 4122-2010 as amended by the client (attached); your own terms do not apply. List any change you propose to the agreement in R6.
- Only a written instruction from the client's representative authorises extra scope, work beyond an allowance or a fee change; work without one is not paid.
- Each stage ends at client sign-off, which sets the baseline for later stages. Design development within the brief is not a variation; a client change after sign-off is assessed under the agreement.
- Correcting your own errors, or coordinating with information you were given, is not a variation.
- Invoice monthly against stage progress; payment within 30 days, not dependent on any authority approval.
- Your proposal stays valid for 90 days.
- Questions in writing to Project manager, pm@example.com by 2026-10-23; answers go to every tenderer as numbered addenda.
- Acceptance by conduct does not adopt your terms.
- No provisional sums: price the allowances. Work that depends on an uninvestigated condition is priced as an option.

### 7. Evaluation

Price 40% · Relevant experience 20% · Team 20% · Methodology and program 10% · Compliance with the returnable schedules 10%. Lowest price does not automatically win.
